newsitem.title: UK: Powell Duffryn disposes of U.S. terminal.
newsitem.headline: Powell Duffryn disposes of U.S. terminal.

text.p: British ports and engineering group Powell Duffryn Plc said it agreed to sell a U.S. chemical terminal for 6.0 million stg cash to IMTT, a venture of the Netherlands' Koninklijke Van Ommeren NV and U.S. group International Tank Terminals.
The sale of the Bayonne, New Jersey, operation followed Powell's disposal of terminals in Savannah, Georgia, the UK and South Africa.

"The Bayonne disposal is a further significant step in the implementation of Powell Duffryn's strategy and substantially reduces group exposure to environmental liabilities in the U.S.," the company said in a statement.
Powell said its maximum liability in respect of any contamination of adjacent sites that occurred during its ownership was limited to 6.0 million stg.

"Powell Duffryn is not aware of any condition which would give rise to such exposure," it said. Powell said the loss on the disposal of the Bayonne terminal would be covered by its previously-announced 11.5 million stg charge taken for all three of its U.S. terminals taken in the first half.
Completion of the transaction was expected within weeks.
